reviews.comment: Very caring professor and you can tell he cares through his work and dedication. He also replies to emails very quickly.

30% of the grade is homework (unlimited attempts) and attendance, and only one final exam (20%) at the end of the semester. Other 50% was quizzes. He's a good prof and teaches the material well. I liked the way he set up his class, but he's very monotone and lectures are hard to pay attention to.

Best choice for CVEN 305. Lots of in class examples. Easy to communicate with and responds quickly to emails. Overall good content in class, will answer any questions and explain in full detail.Fantastic rubric: 10% attendance, 20% homework (multiple submissions), 50% weekly quizzes - if you go to class and do homework you will do well, 20% final.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a good guy, but this course is a nightmare. There is so much work between labs and lectures. Test averages were low; you need to remember the most random facts. He doesn't really post example problems to reference. Lecture attendance is required. After every weekly lab, I would have to go home and pass out because this class is so exhausting.

Dr. Kim is a nice guy and the class was okay but definitely not my favorite professor ever. For the first exam he told us formulas would be provided when all he gave was "derivation formulas". His exams are okay with a formula sheet but be prepared to memorize a lot of terms. There were also pop quizzes and he randomly calls on people in class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is a solid choice for CVEN 305. I had him through zoom classes and I thought his notes were overall very well organized (he posts both his blank powerpoint notes and the annotated version from class). Didn't go too fast during lectures and answered questions. Weekly quizzes worth most of grade. Can tell he wants you to do well and help.
